title: Reversible whole-animal biostasis

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a way to place an intact adult animal from a species without natural cryptobiosis into prolonged, reversible metabolic suspension and then recover that same animal. Recovery would include coordinated movement, feeding, and fertility, rather than survival of scattered cells or restoration of one organ. The defining advance is continuity of the integrated animal across storage: its tissues must remain capable of functioning together when activity resumes.

Two experimental precedents motivate this goal at different biological scales. A tardigrade protein, CAHS D, can form reversible fibrillar networks associated with metabolic suppression and protection of cells during osmotic stress. Separately, isolated rat kidneys have been vitrified, stored cryogenically, rewarmed, and transplanted into living recipients whose survival depended on those kidneys. These establish useful component capabilities, but neither supplied study demonstrates prolonged suspension and recovery of an intact adult vertebrate.

significance.text: As a conditional scientific assessment, successful recovery of behavior and fertility after prolonged whole-animal suspension would establish control over a fundamental feature of animal life: the ability to interrupt and resume integrated physiological activity. It would also create an experimental system for studying how tissues tolerate metabolic arrest and how coordinated function returns. Natural tardigrade biostasis supplies a biological precedent, while the kidney work demonstrates that prolonged preservation can retain an organ’s life-sustaining function.

A plausible direct consequence would be banking research animals of the demonstrated species without maintaining them in an actively feeding and reproducing state throughout the storage interval. This could change colony maintenance and the timing of experiments. Conservation banking of endangered animals would be a further possibility, conditional on species-specific validation, acceptable recovery rates, preserved reproductive capacity, and practical storage costs. Success in one adult species would not establish applicability to other species, developmental stages, repeated suspension cycles, or much longer storage.

The organ-banking analogy is useful because preservation can separate the timing of biological availability from the timing of use. Its limit is equally important: the kidney experiment restored an isolated organ within an already living recipient, which supplied the rest of the physiological system. Whole-animal biostasis would require recovery of that supporting system as well. It would not by itself demonstrate prevention of aging during active life, nor would behavioral recovery alone establish preservation of previously learned memories.

missing_breakthrough.text: The capability still to be demonstrated within the supplied evidence is reversible suspension at the scale of the same intact adult animal. Cellular protection under osmotic stress does not establish that every essential tissue can tolerate prolonged storage. Likewise, a kidney that recovers after transplantation does not establish that an animal’s brain, circulation, respiration, digestive system, and reproductive system can all survive suspension and restart together. The two studies therefore identify relevant starting points without closing the organism-scale gap.

Engineering synthesis: an effective method would need to induce a protective state throughout heterogeneous tissues, maintain that state during storage, and reverse it without disabling any system required for recovery. If a cryogenic route were used, concrete problems would include distributing protective treatments, controlling cooling and rewarming across the body, and avoiding preservation-related injury. If a protein-mediated or desiccation-based route were pursued, the central question would be whether cellular protection could be extended across tissues with different physiological requirements. The supplied results do not establish which route, or combination of routes, could solve these problems.

A further scientific barrier is defining and measuring suspension. Reduced activity, immobility, and reduced metabolism are different observations; none alone establishes complete metabolic arrest. The CAHS D result concerns metabolic suppression during osmotic stress, followed by recovery, rather than proof of zero metabolism. A whole-animal demonstration would need measurements that establish the depth and duration of suppression and identify any residual biological maintenance required during storage.

current_state.text: Sanchez-Martinez and colleagues’ study, “Labile assembly of a tardigrade protein induces biostasis,” appeared online on 19 March 2024 and in Protein Science 33(4), e4941, on 1 April 2024. The supplied repository abstract reports that CAHS D forms labile gels and reversible fibrillar networks, improves survival of cells exposed to osmotic shock, and reduces metabolic activity during that stress. Metabolic rates return to control levels after the fibers resolve. These are cellular protection and reversible metabolic-suppression findings, not demonstrations of complete metabolic arrest or prolonged intact-animal storage.

The CAHS D evidence available to the supplied review was the repository abstract and bibliographic record. The publisher PDF did not load, and the full paper was not assessed there. The abstract also identifies natural tardigrade survival of desiccation through biostasis, but it does not establish engineered suspension of adult vertebrates or justify generalizing the experimental cellular effects to every tissue in an animal.

Han and colleagues’ Nature Communications article, published on 9 June 2023, demonstrated vitrification and nanowarming of isolated rat kidneys followed by life-sustaining transplantation. Kidneys were stored for 1–100 days at −150 °C. After rewarming, they were transplanted into recipients whose native kidneys were removed, making recipient renal function dependent on the graft. All fresh-control and nanowarmed transplant recipients survived the full 30-day study period. The nanowarmed grafts experienced initial dysfunction over roughly 2–3 weeks before renal recovery; the result therefore should not be described as immediate normal function or evidence of indefinite graft durability.

The kidney study demonstrates recovery of a preserved organ in a living recipient, not revival of the animal from which the kidney was taken. It is the only life-sustaining whole-organ cryopreservation demonstration represented in this source set. Calling it the strongest result across the field would require comparative evidence that was not supplied. The review assessed the main article’s text, including methods and discussion, but did not visually inspect figures or linked supplementary datasets. Supplementary extraction warnings and nearly textless reporting-summary material limit what can be inferred from those materials; they do not invalidate the explicit main-text findings.

Neither supplied study demonstrates recovery of a stored intact adult non-cryptobiotic vertebrate. However, the supplied freshness record contains no search history establishing coverage through 1 November 2026. The evidence therefore supports the dated cellular and organ achievements, while leaving the broader present-day status of whole-animal revival unverified. This limitation is not evidence that later demonstrations do or do not exist.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: induce an intact adult animal into a defined state of metabolic suspension, maintain that same animal for at least 30 days without continuous physiological life support, and then recover locomotion, feeding, and fertility over a prespecified follow-up period. An adult zebrafish or mouse could be a candidate model, provided its relevant baseline storage tolerances are established rather than assumed. Thirty days is a proposed threshold for this record, not a published consensus standard. The supplied sources do not independently establish these species’ natural desiccation or cryogenic tolerances.
completion_criteria.label: Whole-animal recovery after ≥30-day suspension without continuous physiological life support

completion_criteria.text: Proposed measurements should quantify metabolic suppression during storage, with stated detection limits, and distinguish suppression from inactivity alone. The protocol should define permitted infrastructure, including temperature control, separately from continuous physiological support. It should also record any assistance needed during induction and recovery. The kidney study’s storage at −150 °C illustrates why freedom from physiological life support should not be confused with freedom from storage equipment.
completion_criteria.label: Metabolic suppression quantified with detection limits and infrastructure distinguished from support

completion_criteria.text: Proposed recovery assessment should compare treated animals with appropriate untreated and procedure controls, report failures as well as successes, and follow survivors long enough to detect delayed impairment. Fertility should be demonstrated through successful reproduction rather than inferred solely from reproductive anatomy or biomarkers. Claims about retained learning or memory would require separate tests of information acquired before suspension. Survival of isolated cells or a transplanted organ would not satisfy the whole-animal endpoint.
completion_criteria.label: Controlled whole-animal recovery assessment demonstrates reproduction and tracks delayed impairment

completion_criteria.text: Convincing reproducibility would require repeated cohorts and independent replication with sufficiently specified induction, storage, and recovery procedures. Results should state the demonstrated species, age range, storage interval, recovery rate, functional outcomes, and infrastructure requirements. Longer storage, repeated cycles, other developmental stages, and other species would each extend the demonstrated scope only when tested. Even a successful finite program would establish breadth within those boundaries, not universal reversibility across animals or unlimited storage duration.
completion_criteria.label: Repeated cohorts and independent replication with reported scope and procedures

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: ZOO-03, “Negligible senescence as an installed life-history program,” concerns maintaining function during active life as an animal ages. ZOO-07 concerns surviving an interval of suspension and resuming activity afterward. A successful storage interval would not establish negligible senescence after recovery. ZOO-02, “Complete limb regeneration in an adult mammal,” concerns rebuilding lost anatomy; biostasis instead requires preservation and recovery of an existing animal. Repair might eventually assist recovery, but it would be an additional capability.

Roster-based synthesis: ZOO-04, “Self-sustaining populations reconstructed from extinct animal species,” overlaps with the conservation motivations of animal banking. Biostasis could preserve living individuals if validated in the relevant species, whereas ZOO-04 requires reconstruction and establishment of a reproducing population. ZOO-01, “A fertile animal booted from a chemically synthesized genome,” and ZOO-10, “Fertile adulthood from a vertebrate cell line, with no gestational parent,” concern producing a new animal from different starting materials. ZOO-07 requires recovery of the same animal that entered storage.

Roster-based synthesis: ZOO-08, “Experimental origin of animal multicellular development,” concerns how animal development can arise, while ZOO-09, “A heritable body plan the ancestor never had,” concerns inherited anatomical novelty. Adult-animal suspension establishes neither developmental origins nor a new body plan. Although suspension might become a tool for developmental experiments, success in adults would not show that embryos, larvae, or other developmental stages can be paused and resumed safely.

Roster-based synthesis: ZOO-06, “A germline-transmitted photosynthetic organelle in an animal,” concerns a heritable addition to animal energy biology. ZOO-07 concerns tolerating prolonged suppression of integrated activity; it neither requires photosynthesis nor demonstrates inheritance of a protective mechanism. ZOO-05, “Two-way semantic communication with another animal species,” concerns shared meaning in interspecies exchange. Recovery of coordinated behavior after storage would not establish semantic communication, and neither outcome would alone prove retention of specific pre-storage memories.

change_log.change: Preserved ZOO-07 and its whole-animal identity while defining recovery of the same intact adult animal as the central requirement.
change_log.reason: Cell survival and organ transplantation are relevant precedents but do not demonstrate continuity of the integrated animal.

change_log.change: Replaced categorical claims of present-day impossibility and an undocumented negative literature search with statements bounded to the supplied studies.
change_log.reason: The supplied freshness record is empty and does not establish field-wide status through 1 November 2026.

change_log.change: Expanded the CAHS D account to distinguish reversible network formation, metabolic suppression, cellular protection, and metabolic recovery from complete arrest.
change_log.reason: These distinctions preserve the useful mechanism without overstating what the repository abstract demonstrates.

change_log.change: Added kidney storage of 1–100 days at −150 °C, the 30-day recipient follow-up, and initial dysfunction lasting roughly 2–3 weeks.
change_log.reason: The reviewed main text supports these quantitative boundaries and prevents an implication of immediate normal function or indefinite durability.

change_log.change: Removed the strongest-result ranking and retained the kidney study as the sole life-sustaining whole-organ example in the supplied source set.
change_log.reason: No comparative evidence supports a ranking across the field.

change_log.change: Qualified conservation applications, developmental generalization, repeated suspension, longer storage, aging effects, and memory preservation.
change_log.reason: These consequences require evidence beyond success in one adult-animal model.

change_log.change: Made the 30-day criterion explicitly proposed and added metabolic measurements, infrastructure definitions, recovery follow-up, and replication.
change_log.reason: The original criterion needed operational boundaries; the clinical-hypothermia comparison and species-tolerance assertions lacked supplied support.

change_log.change: Integrated access limitations and explained distinctions from every other supplied roster entry.
change_log.reason: Readers need to understand the evidence available to the review and how ZOO-07 remains a separate innovation.

unresolved_issues: Whether any later study demonstrates prolonged suspension and recovery of an intact adult non-cryptobiotic vertebrate remains unverified because no freshness search record was supplied.
The full CAHS D paper was unavailable to the supplied review; details beyond its repository abstract cannot be established here.
Figures and linked supplementary datasets in the kidney study were not visually inspected, and some supplementary extraction was incomplete.
The relevant natural storage tolerances of adult zebrafish and mice require independent support before either is treated as an established non-cryptobiotic test model for a particular protocol.
No quantitative definition of metabolic suspension, acceptable recovery rate, follow-up duration, or permitted recovery assistance has been established for the proposed demonstration.
The route to whole-animal protection, the limits on storage duration, and the feasibility of repeated cycles, memory retention, and cross-species extension remain open.

brief.title: Pausing and restarting an adult animal’s life
possible: Researchers could store an intact adult animal with its life processes suspended, then recover that same animal able to move, feed and reproduce. This would extend prolonged, reversible suspension to a species that cannot naturally do it.
why: Research colonies could be stored without keeping animals actively feeding and breeding throughout the wait. This could change colony maintenance and the timing of experiments.
Scientists could study how tissues endure a pause in life processes and resume working together. Conservation programmes could eventually gain another way to bank endangered animals.

sources.showed: CAHS D, a protein from microscopic animals called tardigrades, formed reversible networks of fibres in stressed cells. These improved survival and reduced metabolism, the chemical activity that sustains life. Metabolism returned to normal after the fibres dissolved.
sources.quote: Importantly, CAHS D's fibrillar network formation is reversible and metabolic rates return to control levels after CAHS fibers are resolved.
sources.cited_for: The study supports reversible slowing of cell metabolism linked to protection during sudden changes in water balance.
sources.not_established: The experiments did not establish complete metabolic arrest or prolonged storage and recovery of an intact adult animal.

sources.showed: Rat kidneys survived storage for up to 100 days after cooling into an ice-free, glass-like state. Nanowarming, heating with tiny magnetic particles, restored transplantable kidneys. They sustained recipients’ lives, though kidney function was initially impaired.
sources.quote: Full renal function was restored after nanowarming and transplantation, with the transplanted organs sustaining the life of the recipient animals.
sources.cited_for: The study supports prolonged organ preservation followed by recovery of life-sustaining function.
sources.not_established: The kidneys recovered inside already living recipients; the donor animals were not revived.

shown: Sanchez-Martinez’s team demonstrated reversible protection at the cell scale; Han’s team recovered functioning stored organs. Neither experiment suspended and recovered the same intact adult animal.
missing: A method must protect every essential tissue through storage and allow the brain, circulation, breathing, digestion and reproduction to restart together.
Measurements must establish how deeply and how long metabolism is suppressed, including any biological maintenance that continues during storage.
Whole-animal recovery must include successful reproduction and follow-up for delayed harm, with reproducible results.

milestones.label: Whole-animal recovery after at least 30 days
milestones.explanation: An intact adult animal would have to resume movement, feeding and fertility after at least 30 days of suspension without continuous physiological life support. This would establish continuity of the same animal across storage.

milestones.label: Measured metabolic suppression with clearly defined support
milestones.explanation: Measurements would have to state detection limits, separate storage equipment from continuous life support, and record help during induction and recovery. This would distinguish metabolic suspension from mere inactivity.

milestones.label: Controlled recovery with reproduction and delayed harm assessed
milestones.explanation: Comparisons with untreated and procedure controls would have to report failures, successful reproduction and delayed impairment. This would establish functional recovery; retained learning would require separate tests.

milestones.label: Repeated success and independent replication with defined scope
milestones.explanation: Repeated groups and independent teams would have to reproduce recovery using specified procedures, reporting species, ages, storage time, success rates, function and equipment. This would establish reliability within tested limits.

uncertain: The depth of suppression, acceptable recovery rate, follow-up duration and permitted recovery assistance still need agreed definitions.
It remains unclear which preservation route could protect all tissues and how long that protection could last.
Success in one species would leave other species, repeated suspension cycles and preservation of learned memories open.

page.title: Reversible whole-animal biostasis
page.definition: An intact adult animal from a species without natural cryptobiosis—reversible metabolic arrest—can be stored with metabolism arrested and then recovered as the same animal, able to move in a coordinated way, feed and reproduce.

goal.need: Preservation seeks to separate biological deterioration from the time needed to obtain treatment. DARPA notes that the window for intervention after trauma can be less than 60 minutes. At organ scale, rat kidneys stored for 1–100 days at −150 °C have supported transplant recipients for 30 days. Whole-animal biostasis extends the preservation question to the coordinated recovery of an entire animal.

statements.quote: eventually scaling all the way up to the level of a complete organism.
statements.context: The Biostasis programme described extending reversible biochemical slowing from simpler systems to whole organisms.

statements.quote: reversible whole-body vitrification in a mammal
statements.context: The CRYORAT project, initiated on 25 November 2024, identifies this as necessary for low-temperature human suspended animation. Vitrification is solidification without ice formation.

statements.quote: Human cryopreservation with demonstrable long-term recovery of the whole intact person
statements.context: Brian Wowk's research hierarchy, published on 2 April 2025, defines its final level this way; it assigns no numerical meaning to long-term.

completion.title: A stored adult animal recovers movement, feeding and fertility after induced metabolic arrest.
completion.criterion: The same intact adult animal of a species without natural cryptobiosis undergoes induced whole-body metabolic arrest for a measured storage interval, then recovers coordinated movement, independent feeding and the ability to produce viable offspring. Measurements with stated detection limits distinguish arrest from metabolic slowing. No minimum storage interval, recovery fraction or follow-up duration is assigned because no external threshold for these was located.
completion.basis: Searches of DARPA Biostasis criteria, the 2024 biostasis roadmap, Biostasis Technologies' 2025 hierarchy, CRYORAT milestones and Brain Preservation Prize criteria found no test combining adult whole-animal metabolic arrest, storage and recovered behaviour and fertility. The fallback requires recovery of the same animal; fertility is an Atlas condition. No numerical duration is imposed.

milestones.title: Living cells slow all measurable biological functions and resume activity with minimal damage.
milestones.criterion: A cellular intervention slows all measurable biological functions and permits their return to normal speed with minimal damage. DARPA sets no numerical suppression or duration cutoff. Sanchez-Martinez et al. (19 March 2024) provide partial evidence: human HEK293 cells expressing CAHS D showed reduced metabolic-assay signals under osmotic stress and returned to control levels after 24 hours of recovery; metabolic assays used triplicate wells. This does not establish slowing of every cellular function.
milestones.set_by: DARPA, published Biostasis success conditions, 1 March 2018.
milestones.threshold_quote: the system be slowed across all measurable biological functions

milestones.title: A cryopreserved vital organ sustains a recipient dependent on that transplanted organ.
milestones.criterion: A rewarmed cryopreserved vital organ supports a recipient whose corresponding native organ function is absent. Graft-dependent survival is the test; the experiment's follow-up duration is not a universal cutoff. Han et al. (9 June 2023) stored rat kidneys for 1–100 days at −150 °C. Five nanowarmed-graft recipients and five fresh-graft controls survived 30 days after both native kidneys were removed. Nanowarmed graft function recovered over 2–3 weeks. These were organ transplants, not recovery of stored animals.
milestones.set_by: Organ-cryopreservation research convention: graft-dependent recipient survival, used in rabbit and rat kidney studies discussed by Han et al.
milestones.threshold_quote: Thus, renal function and survival of the animal depended solely on the transplanted organ.

milestones.title: A cryopreserved whole mammalian brain recovers integrated electrical and metabolic function.
milestones.criterion: A cryopreserved whole brain regains normal function. The roadmap's integrated-organ assay uses warm, oxygenated reperfusion after rewarming and cryoprotectant removal, with electrical and metabolic assessment; no numerical cutoff is given. German et al. (3 March 2026) stored mouse brains in situ at −140 °C for 1–8 days. Subsequent hippocampal slices retained long-term potentiation (9 slices, 4 mice); about one-third of protocol iterations yielded evaluable tissue. This is partial tissue recovery, not integrated whole-brain recovery.
milestones.set_by: Biostasis Technologies, Brian Wowk's published research hierarchy, 2 April 2025; operational assay in McKenzie et al.'s research roadmap, section 6.2. This is a developer's research benchmark.
milestones.threshold_quote: Brain cryopreservation with demonstrable return of normal brain function after cryopreservation.

milestones.title: Multiple organs retain viability after whole-body cryopreservation of a mammal.
milestones.criterion: Multiple organs retain biological viability after the animal undergoes whole-body cryopreservation. CRYORAT specifies no organ list, storage temperature, duration or numerical viability cutoff. On 1 September 2025 it reported early recovery signals and EEG activity after ultra-profound hypothermic resuscitation in rats; no cohort size is given. Its update of 13 January 2026 describes multi-organ assay development. These developer updates are not peer reviewed and do not demonstrate this cryopreservation milestone.
milestones.set_by: CryoDAO and Advanced Neural Biosciences, CRYORAT research plan, milestone 4; written for rats.
milestones.threshold_quote: Results that multiple organs can be cryopreserved with good viability through whole-body cryopreservation.

not_found: No numerical acceptance threshold was located for normal whole-brain function or CRYORAT's multi-organ viability milestone.
No published demonstration meeting the whole-animal completion criterion was located.
The proposed mouse Z-PRIZE webpage returned an access error; its full rules could not be checked.

results.finding: CAHS D-expressing HEK293 cells showed reduced metabolic signals and returned to control levels after 24 hours; assays used triplicate wells.
results.detail: The cells were subjected to osmotic stress. The findings do not establish slowing of every measurable cellular function or minimal damage across all functions.
results.quote: Importantly, CAHS D's fibrillar network formation is reversible and metabolic rates return to control levels after CAHS fibers are resolved.

results.finding: Five rat recipients of cryopreserved, nanowarmed kidneys survived 30 days.
results.detail: Both native kidneys were removed. Graft function initially declined, then recovered to control levels over 2–3 weeks.
results.quote: Postoperatively, all fresh control and nanowarmed kidney transplants continued to produce urine, and all animals survived for the full 30-day study period.

results.finding: MCF10A spheroids in 3 replicate wells were 23±7% smaller than controls before photodegradation; their size became comparable to controls after recovery.
results.detail: Intracellular gelation also reduced metabolic measures. Following light exposure, spheroid proliferation recovered, but the study did not establish that every cellular function slowed and returned to normal speed with minimal damage.
results.quote: After exposure to light and subsequent de-gelation, cell proliferation over 10 days resulted in spheroids that were comparable in size to controls.

results.finding: One of three recipients of vitrified, rewarmed rabbit kidneys survived 17 months.
results.detail: Each recipient depended entirely on the transplanted kidney after removal of the opposite native kidney. The other two recipients survived two and three days.
results.quote: Of three rabbit kidneys vitrified, dielectrically warmed under slightly varying conditions, and then transplanted, one survived long-term with return to normal clinical function (serum creatinine < 2 mg/dL) in the recipient animal still living 17 months later.
